A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing sections and Appendices A–J can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendices K–M.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression experiments, empirical NTK measurements, and protein and UTKFace evaluations in Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds activation, BatchNorm, transformer, and UTKFace feature-similarity analyses in Figures 4–7.

M1.justification: The intervention remains inserting LayerNorm into a network, with the same NTK framework and normalization operation. The additional activation and transformer experiments test its existing scope rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix M adds next-step prediction of synthetic linear sequences, including evaluation beyond training sequence lengths. The existing scalar regression functions, protein dataset, and UTKFace task and population coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Appendix L adds BatchNorm networks as explicit comparators. Figure 3 adds XGBoost to the protein prediction-distribution and surface-area comparisons, although it already appeared in Table 1. The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix J revise the reported frozen extractor from ResNet-16 to ResNet-18, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Added experiments vary activations and normalization and evaluate a two-layer transformer trained on indices 1–30 and tested on 20–100. Figure 3 changes the analyzed response from absolute error to average prediction; existing splits and Table 3 budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the analyses beyond v1's LayerNorm-placement and empirical-NTK checks. Appendices K–M test activation sensitivity, BatchNorm versus LayerNorm, and transformer extrapolation. Figure 4 adds UTKFace error versus feature-similarity analysis, while Figure 3 replaces the protein error-growth analysis with prediction trends.

E5.justification: Figure 3 changes statistical trend estimation from linear fits to LOWESS, also used in new Figure 4. Seed counts and uncertainty conventions otherwise remain unchanged: five seeds for toy studies, ten for proteins, and 250 for UTKFace, with 95% confidence intervals. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all reported scores, but Figures 4–7 add substantial qualitative findings: errors increase as facial features become less similar to training data, LayerNorm stabilizes extrapolation across additional activations and a transformer, and BatchNorm does not provide the same stabilization. Revised Figure 3 reports prediction trends, including nearly constant XGBoost extrapolation, in place of the previous error curves.

T1.justification: The assumptions, principal theorems, Proposition 3.4, and mathematical extensions and proofs in Appendices A–I are retained. The LayerNorm formula added to Section 2 restates the operation already defined in Appendix A.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and central conclusions retain their meaning and scope: LayerNorm bounds extrapolation under the stated theory, with supporting finite-network experiments. The added experiments support existing claims, and both versions acknowledge that bounded extrapolation need not be accurate.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a biophysical rationale for moderated protein prediction growth and possible XGBoost underestimation. Section 4.1 adds a BatchNorm/NTK explanation, and the conclusion connects extrapolation limitations to kernel selection and RKHS assumptions. Section 4.3 removes the explicit reminder that different LayerNorm placements need not yield identical predictions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, revises the documented UTKFace extractor, and specifies the new transformer's two layers, four heads, embedding size 64, and sequence-generation process. Existing hardware, initialization, optimizer, timing, and Table 3 settings are retained. The transformer training budget is not specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cleveland's LOWESS reference and four works concerning Gaussian processes, kernel selection, or unknown hyperparameters: Berkenkamp et al., Lloyd et al., and two Ziomek et al. papers. Existing related-work comparisons and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections, rewrites experimental discussion in Sections 4.2–4.3, adds a short LayerNorm explanation, and appends Sections K–M. The main narrative order and theoretical appendix organization remain intact; the front-page publication notice also changes.

P2.justification: The empirical visual presentation expands substantially through new Figures 4–7, including activation and normalization panels and a transformer plot. Figure 3 changes its response axis, curves, caption, and comparator legend. Figure 4 introduces text wrapping within Related Work. Figures 1–2 and the three tables retain their content and basic structure.

improvement.justification: The activation and normalization controls, transformer example, and UTKFace similarity analysis strengthen empirical support for the retained theory, while the code link improves reproducibility information. The theoretical core and main benchmark scores remain unchanged. Benefits are limited by incomplete transformer training details, Figure 4's prediction-versus-error caption inconsistency, and replacement of the direct protein error-versus-size diagnostic.
